DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 97 s. 2021 19 July 2021 HON. REBECCA S. MABULAY Acting Vice-Mayor San Sebastian, Samar Dear Acting Vice-Mayor Mabulay: This has reference to your letter dated 08 June 2021 requesting clarification regarding the source of fund for the salary of the newly designated Sangguniang Bayan Member, Ms. Lea B. Amatosa insofar as AO 15 and DILG MC No. 2019-21 are concerned, citing the following arguments: a-Republic Act No. 7160 does not provide for situations wherein a nonelective person or private citizen may be designated to an elective position by virtue of a temporary vacancy in office wherein such temporary vacancy did not or does not cause paralysis or hiatus in the operation of the LGU concerned. b. As a rule, only an incumbent public official or employee may be designated to a government position as may be provided by law. The designation of a private citizen to assume the power and duties and functions of an elective office violates this principle of law. c. Assumption to office into public office is done either by way of election into office or by way of an appointment into office. The only exception is the case of assumption into office for an ex-officio position, which in reality is acquired either through election or appointment as may be provided by law. d. In the case of temporary vacancies in the sanggunian by virtue of the temporary succession in office of one (1) or more members of the sanggunian, the officer performing the functions of a higher office does not and is not entitled to receive regular compensation/salary of the higher office he/she is temporarily occupying. e. In connection with the preceding argument on the designation of a private citizen (designee) to assume office on the temporary vacancy in the sanggunian by virtue of the temporary successions to higher officer Of one or more members of the local sanggunian may be deemed to be legally infirm. This is the reason that appropriations for the sanggunian positions are actually disbursed and claimed by the duly-elected regular members of the sanggunian. The designation of

a private citizen to a temporary vacancy creates a situation wherein the said designee will not be entitied to receive any compensation from the LGU for the reason and on the fact that all the appropriations were already allocated to and claimed by the regular members of the sanggunian when the law only provides for eight (8). Thus, there is no legal basis for the payment and/or release of such compensation may tantamount to technical malversation at the very least. f. In closing, the temporary vacancy of one (1) SB member will not cause paralysis or hiatus in the Sanggunian or in the local government unit concerned and the situation is aggravated by the fact that fund allocation in the budget allows only for eight (8) regular member's and ex-officio's in accordance with the provision of the Local Government Code of 1991. Surely the COA will not allow disbursement for the salary of the designee as it would violate COA auditing rules and regulations. The situation can only be remedied if the Acting Municipal Mayor and Acting Vice Mayor will be installed as regular Mayor and Vice Mayor thereby creating a regular vacancy in the sanggunian and if they will be allowed to receive the salary of their present designation." It appears that there is a temporary vacancy in the Sangguniang Bayan since you addressed yourself as "Acting Vice-Mayor Rebecca S. Mabulay". This presupposes that Ms. Lea B. Amatosa was designated to fill-in the resultant vacancy in the Sangguniang Bayan resulting from the elevation of the highest ranking sangguniang member or the next highest ranking sanggunian member (in case, the highest ranking sanggunian member is incapacitated to perform). In sum, you are of the view that Ms. Amatosa, the newly designated Sangguniang Bayan Member, might not be given salary as such since: 1. The Local Government Code does not allow private citizens to be designated to an elective position by virtue of a temporary vacancy. As a rule, only an incumbent public official or employee may be designated to a government position; 2. Assumption to public office is only either election to said office of by way of an appointment; 3. The designation of a private citizen to a temporary vacancy creates a situation wherein said designee will not be entitled to receive any compensation from the LGUs since all appropriations were already allocated to and claimed by the regular members of the sanggunian when the law only provides for 8. Thus, there is no legal basis for the payment and/or release of such compensation may tantamount to technical malversation and that COA will not allow disbursement for

the salary of the designee as t would violate COA auditing rules and regulations; 4. After all, the temporary vacancy of 1 SB Member will not cause paralysis or hiatus in the Sanggunian or in the local government unit concerned. In reply to your first, second and fourth arguments, Section 3 of AO 15 reads and we quote: "SECTION 3. Temporary Vacancies in the Sanggunian. (A) Temporary vacancies in the sangquniang panlaiawigan. sanqquniang panlunqsod. sanqgunianq bayan: and sangqunianq baranqay shall be filled by designation by the President. throuqh the SILG or the OIC- DILG. (B) Except for the sanqqunianq barangay. only the nominee of the political party under which the sanqqunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the position next hiqher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be desiqnated in the manner hereinabove provided. The person so desiqnated shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the temporary vacancy and shall serve for the duration of the temporarily vacant office. (C) In case the temporary vacancy is caused by a sanqqunian member who does not belonq to any political party. the President. throuqh the SILG or the OIC-DILG. shall. upon recommendation of the sanqqunian concerned, if still constitutinq a quorum, desiqnate a qualified person to fili the vacancy. (D) In case of temporary vacancies in the representation of the youth and the barangays in the sanggunian, said vacancy shall be filled by designation by the President, through the SILG or the OIC-DILG, of the official next in rank of the organization concerned. (E) In case of temporary vacancies in the sangguniang barangay, the President, through the SILG or the OIC-DILG, shall, upon recommendation of the sangguniang barangay, if still constituting a quorum, designate a qualified person to fill the vacancy." (Emphasis Supplied) AO 15 is clear that temporary vacancy or vacancies in the sangguniang bayan shall be filled-up by the DILG Secretary or Officer-in-Charge, DILG through designation.

Assuming that your arguments were valid, it is settled that unless a law, act or rule, such as AO 15, is annulled in a direct proceeding, it is presumed validl. As to your third argument regarding the absence/lack of basis for the receipt of compensation by Ms. Amatosa, as earlier mentioned, there is a vacancy in the sanggunian. As such and contrary to your allegations, while appropriations for the salaries of the 8 regular members may have been made, the same cannot be fully claimed as one of the positions is declared vacant, that is, no one is in possession of such office in the meantime. Assuming that your argument regarding the validity of designation of Ms. Amastosa was true, since the latter was actually designated as sanggunian member coupled by her actual discharge of the duties and functions of said office, she can be considered as a de facto officer on the basis of the color of authority to the office, without regard to the good or bad faith possession of such office. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY TH AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARL for Local Government Ls/17 Copy furnished: DIR. KARL CAESAR R. RIMANDO Regional Director, DILG-Region VIII Kanhuraw Hill, Tacloban City 1 G.R. No. 210500, KMU, et al. vs. Hon. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino Ill, et al., 02 April 2019.
